@RepJudyChu @WaysMeansCmte @BloodCancerUtd Welcome to Obamacare brought to you 💯 by the Democratic Party

1/ “1.7 million chronically ill lose coverage the first year, premiums double or triple for 20 million more!”

The same tired socialist con game every time the subsidy spigot wobbles. 

Let’s run the tape:

2/ Adam Smith watched 18th-century governments try to cap grain prices with subsidies. Result every time: artificial shortages, black markets, then brutal spikes when the subsidies ran out. 

ACA tax credits are just corn-law subsidies with better branding. Remove the artificial price control and yes, people finally see the real (distorted) cost—distorted by the same mandates and rating rules you refuse to touch.

3/ Milton Friedman spent decades proving the original sin was government intervention itself: the 1940s tax exclusion for employer plans, state benefit mandates, licensing cartels, certificate-of-need laws. 

Those interventions made healthcare unaffordable long before Obamacare. The ACA response? Pour gasoline on the fire, then hand out tax-credit morphine so no one notices they’re burning. Pulling the morphine isn’t the crime; writing the prescription was.

4/ Thomas Sowell would just laugh at the “people cannot survive this” line. His favorite question: “Compared to what?”

Compared to Canada, where 1.2 million are on surgical waiting lists and the median wait from cancer diagnosis to treatment is months?
Compared to the NHS, where leukemia patients get slower access to new drugs than in the U.S. and five-year survival rates are lower?
The vision of compassion that ignores tomorrow’s bigger victims is the cruelest vision of all.

5/ Real-world previews of exactly this movie:

•  Massachusetts 2006 (RomneyCare, the ACA beta test): premiums doubled in five years, state kept having to jack up subsidies and taxes.

•  Britain 1948: Bevan promised the NHS would cost £140 million a year and costs would fall as people got healthier. First-year overrun: 250%. Costs have never stopped rising faster than GDP.
 Every single socialized system runs the same cycle: promise utopia → suppress prices → explode demand → ration care → blame the people who warn it’s coming.

6/ If the enhanced credits expire, premiums don’t “double because Republicans are mean.” They revert to the sky-high level created by community rating, guaranteed issue, and the 10 essential benefits you made untouchable. 

The only sustainable fix is to undo the price controls and cartels—let real insurance return, let states experiment, let cash pricing and competition breathe. Anything else is kicking the can until the whole system collapses under its own weight.

7/ So spare us the crocodile tears at the Ways & Means hearing.
Smith saw this in 1776.
Friedman spelled it out in 1979.
Sowell has been warning about the fatal conceit of “affordability” mandates for fifty years.
You’re not protecting leukemia patients.
You’re protecting the regulatory machine that made leukemia treatment cost half a million dollars in the first place.

History already voted.
Reality is just waiting for the rest of us to catch up.
